findings.title: A rejected device is cached and is allowed on retry
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` adds the device ID to the local cache before attempting the database operation. When the limit has been reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, but the cache entry is retained. The first authentication attempt is rejected, while every subsequent request with that same device ID on this server returns early from the cache and is authenticated without rechecking the limit for roughly 29 minutes. Only cache the ID after a successful write, or remove the entry when the write fails.

findings.title: Anonymous clients can bypass the limit by omitting the device header
findings.body: The limit is enforced only through `TagDevice`, but this method returns success when `X-Grafana-Device-Id` is absent. The anonymous authenticator then issues an anonymous identity normally. Because this is a client-controlled request header, a client can simply omit it (or use a client that never sends it) to obtain unlimited anonymous access regardless of `device_limit`. Enforcing this feature requires rejecting or otherwise accounting for anonymous requests without a server-verifiable device identifier.

findings.title: Device count and insertion are not an atomic limit check
findings.body: The store counts active devices in one database session and, if the result is below the limit, performs the upsert later in a separate session. Concurrent requests for different new device IDs can all observe the same count below the limit and all insert successfully, so the configured limit can be exceeded by an arbitrary number of simultaneous requests (including across Grafana instances). Use a transaction with appropriate locking/serialization or a database-enforced atomic quota operation.
